filename: Atmospheric radiation- using machine learning for the unknowable and uncomputable.pdf
title: Atmospheric radiation: using machine learning for the unknowable and uncomputable
processes: shortwave and longwave radiative flux and heating rate
testbed_rationale: This document is a slide presentation reviewing the history, limitations, and future directions of machine learning for atmospheric radiation; no datasets or benchmark suites are produced or released.
pain_points: Data required to learn 3D radiative effects directly remains sparse due to the computational cost of resolving fine-scale cloud scenes combined with 3D radiative transfer calculations.
Machine learning parameterizations trained on existing 1D parameterizations inherit their physical approximations and systematic errors (abandoning known physical equations).
1D plane-parallel and homogeneous column approximations lead to substantial flux and albedo biases because horizontal transport and subgrid cloud inhomogeneity are neglected.
Large-scale models do not resolve the small-scale features that control 3D radiative effects, posing a representation problem.
extraction_notes: The document is a slide presentation by Robert Pincus discussing past approaches (e.g., Chevallier, Krasnopolsky, Lagerquist, Veerman) and prospective paradigms (e.g., neural adjoints for 4DVar, SPARTACUS calibration and correction of 3D radiative effects, PyTorch-Fortran bindings) in radiative transfer modeling.
